subject: Private deployment: platform fee split, tiering & upgrade credit discussion
messages:
From: Lina Morales <lina@cerebra.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cerebra Health Procurement <procurement@cerebra.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: VPC commercial question — platform fee split & upgrade credits

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. The procurement team at Cerebra finished a first pass at the SOW and we have two items that need clarity before we can sign:

1) Platform fee allocation: your standard private deploy SOW shows a single platform fee. For our internal accounting we need the portion that maps to the managed control plane (hosted control plane services) vs the on-site operator licenses. Can you provide the proposed split (percent / dollar) and whether the hosted portion is amortizable over the contract?

2) Upgrade credits: we expect to expand GPU capacity in Q4; is there a standard approach for granting upgrade credits or prepaid node conversions if we move from a starter bundle to a larger commit within the first 12 months? If so, what are the timing and audit requirements?

I attached our draft SOW and a short usage forecast. Can you loop in finance/solutions so we can get a line-by-line?

Appreciate it — we’d like to get this into legal by the end of next week if possible.

Best,
Lina Morales
Director, Procurement
Cerebra Health
Attachments: Cerebra_VPC_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf), cerebra-usage-forecast-2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Morales <lina@cerebra.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC commercial question — platform fee split & upgrade credits

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Looping in David (finance) and Grace (solutions packaging) — below is a concise starting position so your legal and finance teams have something tangible to review.

Platform fee allocation (starter recommendation):
- Control plane (hosted control plane ops): 35% of platform fee, presented as an amortizable professional/managed service line on the invoice (can be capitalized depending on your accounting).
- On-site entitlement / operator licenses: 65% of platform fee, treated as a licensing/entitlement line.
- We can produce an invoice template that separates the two lines month-to-month or as a one-time activation line — whichever maps to your internal capex/opex preference.

Upgrade credit approach (starter -> committed scale within 12 months):
- If Cerebra upgrades committed nodes within 12 months, Redwood applies a conversion credit equal to 75% of unused starter fee pro-rata toward the new committed node licenses (proof: signed change order + usage snapshot).
- Credits require a 30-day usage reconciliation window and an audit of node counts (we accept your telemetry or our agent logs).
- If the conversion happens after 12 months, standard upgrade pricing applies (no retro credits) but we offer a one-time promotional credit case-by-case for strategic accounts.

Next steps I propose:
1) David — can you confirm the amortization language and whether we can make the hosted control plane explicitly capitalizable on the invoice?
2) Grace — can you prepare a short amendment template (SOW addendum) that codifies the 75% conversion credit and the reconciliation/audit steps?
3) Lina — once we have the amendment and the invoice template we’ll issue a clean commercial redline for legal.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if that speeds things up.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0132

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Lina Morales <lina@cerebra.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC commercial question — platform fee split & upgrade credits

Tessa / Lina — quick confirmation from finance:

- Amortization: Redwood can label the hosted-control-plane line as a professional/managed service that customers typically amortize over the contract term for CAPEX treatment. We will provide wording that explicitly states "Hosted Control Plane — Managed Services (eligible for capitalization under customer policy)" so your accounting team has the necessary descriptor.

- Invoice mechanics: We'll deliver an invoice template that separates Hosted Control Plane and On-site Entitlement as discrete line items. If Cerebra prefers monthly amortization vs one-time activation, we can support both.

- Credit mechanics refinements (Grace to finalize SOW language):
  * 75% pro-rata conversion credit (starter -> committed within 12 months) — confirmed.
  * Credit audit: Redwood requires either (a) telemetry snapshot from Cerebra's monitoring export or (b) a short export from Redwood's agent logs. We accept either; if both are unavailable, a manual spreadsheet can be used with mutually agreed checkpoints.

Lina — finance is comfortable with the approach above. Grace, when you have the amendment draft, please tag me so I can validate the credit calculation example.

Thanks,
David
VP, Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Morales <lina@cerebra.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC commercial question — platform fee split & upgrade credits

Hi Lina — attached is a short SOW amendment (two pages) that implements the items we discussed: explicit invoice line split, the 75% pro-rata conversion credit formula with an illustrative worked example, and the 30-day reconciliation / audit checklist. I also included a sample change order that your legal team can attach to the SOW.

Summary of attached (high level):
- Section A: Invoice split — Hosted Control Plane (35%) vs On-site Entitlement (65%), with a checkbox for "monthly amortization" or "one-time activation".
- Section B: Conversion credit — credit = 0.75 * remaining starter-period platform fee * (remaining months / starter term months). Example given for a 6-month conversion in month 4.
- Section C: Audit & evidence — telemetry export OR Redwood agent log export OR signed reconciliation spreadsheet; Redwood to validate within 10 business days of receipt.
- Section D: Execution flow — change order + PO required to redeem credits; credits applied to subsequent invoice within 30 days post-validation.

If this looks good on your end, I'll convert the amendment to DocuSign and send a completed package. We can also convert the invoice template to a PDF sample for your accounting team.

Lina — proposed next actions:
1) Please confirm you want "monthly amortization" checked on the invoice.
2) If agreed, sign the amendment in DocuSign (I will send link) and we will issue the final commercial redline for your legal team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a brief call if any item needs clarification.

— Grace
Solutions Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SOW_Amendment_for_Cerebra_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
